req.title: Create form GET returns 200
req.statement: The system shall serve the create-post form at GET /create for authenticated users.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that GET /create must return HTTP 200 for authenticated users. Three test cases are designed: (1) positive EP test — authenticated user gets 200; (2) negative NEG test — unauthenticated user is redirected (302) not served the form; (3) boundary STC test — user logs in then immediately hits GET /create, verifying the state transition from anonymous to authenticated yields exactly 200 with form content. Each test uses exact-value assertions to kill status-code mutations (200->201, 302->301, etc.) and checks response body content to kill template-rendering mutations.

tests.name: test_create_get_authenticated_returns_200
preconditions: App is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
User is logged in via POST /auth/login
expected: Response body contains the create-post form (b'<form' present)
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os

def test_create_get_authenticated_returns_200():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    login_r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert login_r.status_code == 302
    r = client.get('/create')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'<form' in r.data

test_create_get_authenticated_returns_200()

tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os

def test_create_get_unauthenticated_returns_302_not_200():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/create')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.status_code != 200
    location = r.headers.get('Location', '')
    assert '/auth/login' in location

test_create_get_unauthenticated_returns_302_not_200()

from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os

def test_create_get_after_login_state_transition_200():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    pre_login = client.get('/create')
    assert pre_login.status_code == 302
    assert pre_login.status_code != 200
    login_r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Anjali', 'password': 'cloud'})
    assert login_r.status_code == 302
    r = client.get('/create')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'<form' in r.data
    assert b'method' in r.data

test_create_get_after_login_state_transition_200()
